audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows disagreed with their own whys and with the packet: Level 1 was Skill while whys[0] says Poppy wins the stat check, Levels 2 and 3 were Malphite while whys[1] and whys[2] call both windows even, Levels 4-5 and 6 were Skill while whys[3] and whys[4] hand both to Malphite, and 2+ items was Malphite while whys[6] says it flattens out.
audit.why: Every stage's prose was already right; the tokens were not, so the chart argued with the text underneath it.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Poppy / Skill / Skill / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite / Skill in matched full/content pairs, ratings rescaled. Identical to the audited malphite__poppy mirror.

audit.why: Four spikes present — level 1 stat check, levels 2-3 wall window, level 6 R, 2+ items tank stall — and they match the corrected chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings tell the player Steadfast Presence cannot stop Unstoppable Force: whys[4] ('your W cannot stop it'), spikes[2].text ('does NOT stop Malphite's R'), the mid text ('it does nothing against his ult, so do NOT count on W'), and wants.foe[2] ('it ignores your W dash-grounding entirely'). Malphite's R is flagged as a dash in his own kit, and Riot's W text says Poppy stops enemy dashes around her and slows and grounds whatever she catches. The full layer's own breakdown.cooldowns already says 'Dash engage — your W can disable it', so the page contradicts itself.
audit.why: This is the single decision the matchup turns on. A Poppy told her W is useless against his engage will spend it on poke and then have nothing when he ults.
audit.corrected: All four strings now say W does catch Unstoppable Force, with the countable caveat that makes it honest advice: W is 20s at rank 1 and 12s at rank 5 against his 130s R, so the answer only exists if you saved it. The early text's 'he has no dash to ground' corrected to 'his only dash is his level-6 R'.

edits.before: W deletes his dash mid-flight — hold it like a parry. Only take the trade when Malphite's Unstoppable Force is down.
edits.after: Hold W for his level-6 R — that is the only dash he has. For now trade around Ground Slam's 7s and Thunderclap's 10s.

edits.before: His R is unstoppable and your W cannot stop it — he flips every all-in at 6, owning this window outright.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is a dash and W does catch it — but W is 20s at rank 1, so if it is spent he flips the all-in.

edits.before: His R unstoppable engage is the real threat — your W grounds dashes but does NOT stop Malphite's R, so he flips the all-in here.
edits.after: His R engage is the real threat, but it is a dash — hold Steadfast Presence for it, and count its 20s before you spend it.

edits.before: Level 6 flips the lane toward him. His R is unstoppable and your W only grounds dashes — it does nothing against his ult, so do NOT count on W to stop his engage. Once he has R he can flip any all-in you start, and his Q slow plus W armor makes him hard to burst down even with your percent-HP Q. Trade with Q max-HP chunks and back off; don't sit in his Q poke waiting for an E angle that isn't there. Bait his R or play around it being on cooldown.
edits.after: Level 6 flips the lane toward him. Unstoppable Force is a dash, so Steadfast Presence does stop it — but W is 20s at rank 1 against his 130s R, so that answer only exists if you saved it instead of spending it on poke. Once he has R he can flip any all-in you start, and his Q slow plus W armor makes him hard to burst down even with your percent-HP Q. Trade with Q max-HP chunks and back off; don't sit in his Q poke waiting for an E angle that isn't there.

edits.before: Pre-6 is your half of the lane. At level 1 his single Q point only chips you, and your higher base HP and armor mean you eat his poke better than he eats yours. Once you hit level 2-3 with Q and E, hunt for an E into the side walls — it's an unconditional stun, and your Q smashes a chunk of his max HP regardless of his armor. Don't waste W here; he has no dash to ground, so hold it. Just respect that his Q slow can kite you off a follow-up if you overcommit without a wall behind him.
edits.after: Pre-6 is your half of the lane. At level 1 his single Q point only chips you, and your higher base HP and armor mean you eat his poke better than he eats yours. Once you hit level 2-3 with Q and E, hunt for an E into the side walls — it's an unconditional stun, and your Q smashes a chunk of his max HP regardless of his armor. Don't waste W here; his only dash is his level-6 R, so hold it. Just respect that his Q slow can kite you off a follow-up if you overcommit without a wall.

edits.before: Save R to flip any all-in you start — it ignores your W dash-grounding entirely
edits.after: Save R to flip any all-in you start, above all while your W is on cooldown

notes: Not asserted: the _missing list claims Granite Shield 'bypasses stacking resistances'. That comes from a percentHealth flag misfire — the passive is a shield sized at 10% of his max health, not percent-health damage — so I wrote no resistance-invalidation claim. The existing advice to itemize magic and percent-HP against his armour stacking is sound on its own and was left alone. Also left alone: dosFull[2].t 'W-tank his Q poke' and dontsFull[0].t 'Auto into his W' are both under 25 characters and skipped by the applier; 'Auto into his W' is genuinely useful given Thunderclap is an auto reset that shields him, but the title cannot be repaired here.
